newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NANTES UPSET BY SECOND DIVISION SIDE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NANTES UPSET BY SECOND DIVISION SIDE.

text.p: Nantes, unbeaten in their previous 17 matches, crashed out of the French League Cup on Sunday when they lost to second division Louhans-Cuiseaux 4-2 on penalties after a 0-0 draw following extra time.
Louhans' upset second round victory left them the only non first division side in the quarter-finals.
Brazilian striker Anderson scored a first half hat-trick as Monaco, who needed a penalty shootout to defeat second division Troyes in the first round, won 3-1 at second division Le Mans.
Anderson, who has a league championship tally of 11 goals, scored in the eighth, 33rd and 39th minutes. Dagui Bakari replied for Le Mans in the 12th.
Holders Metz were eliminated 1-0 by fellow first division Caen, who scored through defender Joachim Fernandez, while Bordeaux, Strasbourg, Lens and Montpellier also reached the last eight.
The remaining second round tie between Rennes and Lyon, who eliminated Paris Saint-Germain in the first round, will be played on Wednesday.
Bordeaux beat Marseille, conquerors of French Cup holders Auxerre in the previous round, at home 1-0 after extra time on Saturday.
Midfielder Michel Pavon converted a 103rd minute penalty and Marseille finished the game with 10 men after Christophe Galtier was sent off for a bad foul on Johan Micoud near the end.
Third division giant-killers Nimes, who reached the French Cup final in May, lost 1-0 at home to Montpellier on Friday and are now out of both domestic cup competitions this season.
